project: Elections — trusted election data sources master list
requirement: Free, publicly available data from official, verified, trusted sources only. Every entry verified line-by-line on 2026-09-18. No hallucinations: every URL below was fetched or corroborated during verification; see data/verification_log.md for per-line evidence.

caveats: Homepage on check date listed 2 sitting commissioners and 4 vacant seats; enforcement-quorum implications flagged for review. Data publication was current (week of Sept 14-18, 2026 digest observed).
sources.description: Independent federal agency. Official campaign finance data, candidate filings, and election-results/voting information hub.
sources.name: Federal Election Commission (FEC)

verification.evidence: Direct page fetch returned live homepage with current items: 'Week of September 14-18, 2026' digest and 'Statistical Summary of 15-Month Campaign Activity of the 2025-2026 Election Cycle'.

sources.description: Independent bipartisan federal commission and the only federal agency solely focused on election administration. Publishes election administration data, voting system guidelines, clearinghouse resources, and the Election Administration and Voting Survey program.
sources.name: U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC)

verification.evidence: Direct page fetch returned live homepage with August 2026 content (National Poll Worker Recruitment Day 2026, Learning Lab certification, 2025 Clearie winners).

sources.description: National Archives / Office of the Federal Register. Official Electoral College process information, Certificates of Ascertainment/Vote, and historical results.
sources.name: National Archives — Electoral College

verification.evidence: Direct page fetch returned live page ('The Electoral College — It is a Process, not a Place') with verified links to results, FAQs, and certificates.

sources.description: Census Bureau Current Population Survey voting supplements. Reported voting and registration by age, sex, race, and state for every national election since 1964. November 2024 detailed (P20) tables released April 2025.
sources.name: U.S. Census Bureau — Voting and Registration

verification.evidence: Search index returned the live topic page with November 2024 tables/publications listed; data sub-page URL observed in the same index record.

sources.description: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House. Official vote counts for President, Senate, House, Resident Commissioner, and Delegates compiled from official state sources; published since 1920. Includes 119th Congress nominees list and Statistics of the 2024 election.
sources.name: Clerk of the U.S. House — Election Information

verification.evidence: Search index returned the live Election Information page describing 119th Congress nominees, Statistics of the 2024 Presidential and Congressional Election, and historical statistics since 1920.

sources.description: MIT Election Data + Science Lab. Practice-oriented election science: Elections Performance Index (2008-2024), Survey of the Performance of American Elections, Election Resource Hub, and an open election-data portal.
sources.name: MIT Election Lab (MEDSL)

verification.evidence: Direct page fetch returned live homepage (EPI 2008-2024, SPAE, data portal link). MIT GitHub org MEDSL corroborates precinct-level official-returns repos (2018/2020/2024).

sources.description: Academic national surveys of voters before/after U.S. elections since 1948; 70+ free datasets, Guide to Public Opinion, question search tools. Run by Michigan/Stanford with Duke and UT-Austin; NSF-funded.
sources.name: American National Election Studies (ANES)

verification.evidence: Direct page fetch returned live homepage (75 Years of ANES, 70+ datasets, free downloads, 2025 site stats). UMich Center for Political Studies page corroborates stewardship.

caveats: Program home migrated from Harvard to Tufts; Harvard pages remain as archive + dataset links. Always cite the DOI/dataverse link actually used.

The url_data DOI (10.7910/DVN/PR4L8P) is the 2022 Common Content release (title confirmed via the Dataverse dataset API on 2026-09-19: version 4, released 2024-04-23, CC0, N = 60,000). Later CES releases have their own DOIs — look them up on the CES dataverse before citing 2024 data.
sources.description: Largest academic survey of the American public (50,000+ respondents in election years, YouGov-administered, NSF-supported). Two-wave pre/post design; data on Harvard Dataverse with DOIs back to 2006.
sources.name: Cooperative Election Study (CES)

verification.evidence: Direct fetch of the Harvard page shows the migration notice pointing to Tufts; direct fetch of the Tufts URL resolves to the live CES research-center page with data-download and analytics links.

sources.access: free, no login for public datasets
caveats: Repository homepage HTML fetch returned HTTP 500 to our checker on 2026-09-18 (transient/rendering issue); API and registry records confirm the repository is live. Re-check homepage in next session.

Re-check 2026-09-19: homepage HTML again HTTP 500 to the fetcher (2 attempts); API /api/info/version OK (6.10.1, build iqss-4) and the dataset API resolves DOIs normally — treat the HTML front-end as unverified-by-machine, the repository as live.
sources.description: Harvard endowed open research-data repository (Institute for Quantitative Social Science). Hosts CES/CCES datasets and much of the world's social-science replication data. Machine-readable API available.
sources.name: Harvard Dataverse

verification.evidence: API info endpoint returned {status: OK, version 6.10.1}; Harvard Library service page and re3data registry record (accessed 2026-09-18) corroborate.

caveats: AP-NORC describes VoteCast in the past tense (conducted 2017-2024); continuation for the 2026 cycle is UNCONFIRMED. Use archived public-use files + ICPSR series until status is re-verified.
sources.description: AP-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research (AP + NORC at the University of Chicago). Probability-based polling, trends, and the AP VoteCast election-survey program with public-use data files.
sources.name: AP-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research

verification.evidence: Direct fetch of homepage returned current September 2026 research; search index returned the VoteCast project page and the ICPSR series page (series 2380).

caveats: Site restructured: legacy /politics/ path no longer resolves; use the verified topic URL.
sources.description: Nonpartisan fact tank. Public-opinion polling, demographic research, and methods transparency (political weighting explainer, Methods 101). Politics & Policy topic hub is the entry point for election research.
sources.name: Pew Research Center — Politics & Policy

verification.evidence: Direct fetch of pewresearch.org root returned live homepage with Sept 15-17, 2026 publications and the Politics & Policy topic link used here.

caveats: Princeton research guide notes Gallup stopped asking a presidential approval question on its surveys as of Spring 2026. Do NOT assume the approval time series continues; verify series-by-series before use.
sources.description: Public-opinion research and analytics. Long-running U.S. and World Poll programs; politics topic hub carries election-related releases.
sources.name: Gallup News

verification.evidence: Direct fetch resolved to /home.aspx with current poll releases and politics topic link. Caveat sourced from Princeton University research guide (libguides.princeton.edu/politics/opinion).

sources.description: Independent nonpartisan university poll (est. 1988). National + 20-state surveys via live-interviewer RDD; AAPOR Transparency Initiative charter member.
sources.name: Quinnipiac University Poll

verification.evidence: Direct fetch returned live homepage with Sept 10 and Sept 16, 2026 poll releases; methodology page corroborated via search index.

sources.description: Marist University survey research center (est. 1978). National/state/local polls, Poll Hub podcast, and a free polling Academy. AAPOR Transparency Initiative charter member.
sources.name: Marist Poll

verification.evidence: Direct fetch returned live homepage with July 1, 2026 poll and Sept 17, 2026 podcast episode; about page corroborated via search index.

caveats: today.yougov.com URLs now redirect to the yougov.com domain; use the verified canonical URL.
sources.description: Online panel pollster. Conducts the weekly Economist/YouGov poll and CES fieldwork; politics content hub carries election coverage and trackers.
sources.name: YouGov — Politics

verification.evidence: Direct fetch of today.yougov.com/politics redirected to live yougov.com politics page featuring the Aug 28-31, 2026 Economist/YouGov poll.

sources.description: Global research firm; conducts the Reuters/Ipsos core political polls and monthly political tracking. U.S. opinion-polls hub carries current releases.
sources.name: Ipsos (Reuters/Ipsos)

verification.evidence: Search index returned the live U.S. opinion-polls hub with Reuters/Ipsos releases dated June-August 2026.

caveats: Direct fetch returned HTTP 200 with the correct page title but a stale (2010-era) snapshot served to the checker; live operation corroborated by a Sept 17, 2026 third-party citation of the RCP average. Freshness must be confirmed by a human visit before use.
sources.description: Poll aggregation and averages across races/agenda items. Long-running 'latest polls' index and race averages.
sources.name: RealClearPolitics — Polls

verification.evidence: Direct fetch: HTTP 200, title 'RealClearPolitics - All Latest Polls', but stale snapshot content. Live status corroborated by third-party citation dated 2026-09-17.

sources.description: UVA Center for Politics (nonpartisan unit founded by Larry Sabato). Free weekly Crystal Ball newsletter + ratings for House, Senate, governor, president, and down-ballot races.
sources.name: Sabato's Crystal Ball (UVA)

verification.evidence: Direct fetch returned live ratings page with current 2026-cycle rating changes (MI, IA, NJ, TX, FL, ME, CA-22, etc.). UVA affiliation corroborated via university and X-profile records.

caveats: Aug 19, 2025 site announcement: exclusive partnership with The Argument; bulk of new analysis is published there. Track both the site and the newsletter; newsletter URL NOT yet verified.
sources.description: Independent elections-analysis and modeling site (co-founded by Lakshya Jain). Candidate-quality research, WAR metric, midterm/presidential modeling, and turnout analysis.
sources.name: Split Ticket

verification.evidence: Direct fetch returned live homepage with 2025-2026 cycle articles (2026 House field, TX redistricting, turnout in 2024). Partnership notice read on the same domain.

sources.access: free, no login for most data
caveats: Premium 'OS Pro' tool exists; core donor/candidate/race data remains free. Federal + state coverage; state depth varies.
sources.description: Center for Responsive Politics (nonpartisan nonprofit). Most comprehensive public database of federal campaign finance: donors, candidates, PACs, outside spending, lobbying, personal finances.
sources.name: OpenSecrets

verification.evidence: Direct fetch returned live homepage with Sept 16, 2026 news and full data-navigation (politicians, elections, lobbying). Stewardship corroborated by MacArthur grantee record.

verification_policy: Statuses: verified-live (fetched live content on check date), search-corroborated (live content observed via search index on check date), verified-exists-freshness-unconfirmed (URL resolves but freshness needs human confirmation), api-plus-registry, fetch-plus-third-party. Anything else is NOT admitted to this file.
